request.spec:
Add an audit viewer to the screen: a filter entry, a show button and a list of lines. With the
filter blank it lists every audit line of this sheet exactly as the file holds it, newest first.
With a name in the filter it lists only the lines about that person: those carrying name=<the
name> or person=<the name>, compared as names are compared (case and surrounding spaces ignored).
The viewer reads what the file holds; it is not a second record.

agent.result_text:
The audit viewer is on the screen and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

It has a filter box (`audit-filter`), a Show button (`audit-show`) and the list of lines (`audit-line`):
- **Blank filter:** it lists every line of this sheet exactly as the audit file holds it, newest first.
- **A name in the filter:** it lists only the lines carrying `name=<name>` or `person=<name>`, ignoring case and surrounding spaces. Lines that mention the person another way, such as `patron=Ben`, are not included.

The viewer re-reads the file each time you press Show, and nothing is stored or audited separately. If the request fails, the error shows in `audit-error`.

What I changed:
- **Server:** a new route `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/audit?name=…` (`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/audit.GET.yml`). It is handled by three small classes in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/audit/`, plus a `read(sheetId, name)` method added to the existing `Audit` service that does the filtering.
- **Front end:** `src/main/frontend/features/audit/audit.slot.tsx`, which adds the viewer to the sheet. Typing in the filter or pressing Show clears the old list first, so two presses are always distinguishable.

The name match compares whole space-separated words. A line where the name itself contains a space (e.g. `name=Ada Lovelace`) would not match. None of the test data has such names.
